candidate.answerReason: The total distance is 180 miles and the full elapsed time, including the stop, is four hours. Their quotient is 45 miles per hour.

methods.label: Divide total distance by total time
methods.explanation:
Average speed is the total distance divided by the total elapsed time. The stop adds time to the trip but adds no distance, so it must be included in the four-hour total.

The car travels \(80+100=180\) miles altogether. Its average speed is therefore
\[
\frac{180\text{ miles}}{4\text{ hours}}=45\text{ miles per hour}.
\]
The answer is \(45\) miles per hour, choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
methods.levelReason: The method uses the elementary definition of average speed and a single whole-number division.

candidate.annotationRationale: The available division-application node cnm_p084 captures interpreting 180 divided by four as miles per hour. Combining the journey's distances uses cnm_p035. The essential whole-trip average-speed definition, particularly inclusion of stopped time, is proposed separately because the catalog's forward distance formula does not state it.

needsNewNodes.name: Average speed over an entire journey
needsNewNodes.description: Calculate average speed as total distance divided by positive total elapsed time. Combine all journey segments and include stopped time in the elapsed time.
needsNewNodes.reason: The catalog contains forward distance-speed-time relationships and contextual division, but no explicit target for whole-trip average speed including stops.
